chunks: From him, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Miskān, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Khāliq, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the time of ẓuhr, so he said: After the sun’s decline by a foot’s length or something near that, except on Friday or during travel, for its time then is when the sun declines.

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: the sun’s decline from the meridian, marking the start of noon prayer time
key_terms.بِقَدَمٍ: by the measure of a foot; a traditional indicator of elapsed shadow length
key_terms.تَزُولُ الشَّمْسُ: the sun declines from its midpoint in the sky
key_terms.فِي السَّفَرِ: during travel, where the prayer time begins earlier
key_terms.وَقْتِ الظُّهْرِ: the prescribed time of the ẓuhr prayer
key_terms.يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, for which an exception in timing is stated

ai.seo_question: When does the time of ẓuhr prayer begin according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding the beginning time of ẓuhr prayer. It indicates that the usual time is after zawāl by the measure of a foot or close to it, while on Friday and during travel its time begins immediately at the sun’s decline.
